name: Unify plan-scoped routing and user navigation
description:
Create one coherent user-facing application flow from the seeded/shared plan link through schedule, calendar, fixture detail, duty claim, and personal cockpit. The current implementation is split between the canonical link-first routes under /plans/:planId and legacy global routes such as /dashboard, /assignments, /team-list, and /cockpit. This makes the calendar feature unreachable from a seed link and prevents reliable end-to-end workflow testing.

The epic must first inventory and document the behavior currently provided by the disconnected routes so useful behavior is not lost. Then define and implement one canonical plan-scoped route/navigation contract, migrate or re-wire existing surfaces into it, and remove the global legacy routes. Seeded links must enter the same flow users follow thereafter.

Accepted decisions:
- /plans/<planId> is the schedule entrypoint with one timeline/calendar toggle.
- Plan-dependent routes are /plans/<planId>/matches/<matchId>, /cockpit, /teams, /assignments, and /setup.
- Timeline, calendar, stats, filtering, member duties filtering, iCal export, assignment management, and team/member management are preserved; check-in is removed.
- Cockpit owns member selection. Claiming without a selection opens a dialog, persists the choice, and resumes the claim. Fixture detail does not contain member selection.
- Regular navigation is read/claim-focused. Admin navigation will be prototyped as both a shared shell and a separate Manage shell; the chosen design is a UX boundary only, never authorization.
- /setup and /plans/<planId>/setup are explicit reachable placeholders until the separate setup epic implements them.
- There are no accounts or real identities. The shared key remains in URL fragments, including direct shared nested links.

Success criteria:
- A fresh seed link opens the canonical schedule surface with current plan data.
- One consistent navigation flow reaches schedule/calendar, fixture detail, claim, cockpit, teams, and assignment/admin surfaces.
- Existing disconnected-route behavior is documented with an explicit disposition before removal.
- No route renders fallback/example data when a plan-scoped route lacks valid plan data.
- At least one deterministic end-to-end browser release gate exists for each major workflow.

The separate setup epic owns new-plan creation, existing-plan editing, finalization, and sharing. The wireframe-alignment task follows the member-route migration.

name: Minimize encrypted plan payload before chunking
description:
Measure whether minifying serialized SeasonPlan JSON reduces encrypted payload size enough to avoid Deno KV chunking for representative current and large seeded plans. Preserve the opaque encrypted blob contract and keep chunking for payloads that remain above the storage limit. Verify existing encrypted plans still load, decrypt, and migrate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Record before/after payload sizes for at least one normal and one large seeded plan.
- Add a regression test or documented threshold check for serialization size.
- Existing encrypted fixtures remain readable.
- Chunking behavior remains correct when the minimized payload still exceeds the limit.
- Document whether minification materially reduces chunking frequency and avoid speculative format changes.

name: Define JSON command contract and domain boundary
description:
Define the smallest stable JSON contract between the command runner and plan operations. Commands receive decrypted SeasonPlan JSON and explicit command input; they never call Pinia, Vue, browser storage, SSE, or HTTP. Mutation responses are compact by default so callers can perform get -> mutate -> get again; reserve a future low-priority --full option for returning the complete updated plan.

Contract must define:
- validate, claim-duty, auto-assign, and complete-assignments requests.
- Success response shape, compact mutation result shape, and error response shape.
- Error categories and process exit behavior.
- stdin and/or file input behavior.
- Explicit clock input for time-dependent completion.
- Mapping from current store/utilities to commands.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each command has valid request and response examples.
- Invalid JSON, invalid plans, unknown commands, and rejected domain actions have distinct documented failures.
- The boundary and unresolved assumptions are documented before implementation begins.

name: Migrate member workflow into plan-scoped routes

Put the existing timeline/calendar schedule at /plans/:planId with one view toggle; preserve filtering, stats, member duties filtering, and iCal export while removing check-in. name: Add calendar feeds and downloads
description: Define and implement calendar delivery for the canonical plan-scoped schedule and member cockpit. This is separate from the existing browser-only member export and must work with the link-first encrypted-plan model without exposing the decryption key to the server. Settled design, recorded in ADR 0009: use one canonical encrypted plan blob; create stateless encrypted HTTPS feed tokens; include plan scope, optional member scope, expiry, and wrapped plan key; decrypt the current blob in memory per request; support matches (all timeline matches, no assignments) and member-duties (selected member only); place full-plan download on the schedule and member download in the cockpit; use UTC for match instants; avoid token/plaintext/ICS logging and use conservative no-store caching; defer per-token revocation. Remaining work: implement the read-only webcal feed and full-plan/cockpit ICS delivery paths, with focused tests and canonical plan-scoped UI actions. Out of scope: authentication/accounts, two-way calendar sync, schedule import, and legacy global routes.

name: Align slot model and assignment invariants

Requirements:
- Use explicit assignmentStatus values OPEN, ASSIGNED, COMPLETED, and CANCELLED.
- Assigned duties become completed after the gameday closing time; users do not check in.
- Preserve helperTeamId as a presentation/allocation preference, not a hard claim restriction.
- Define shared capability eligibility using Role.requiredSkillId and Member.skillIds.
- Add or update migration logic for existing example and persisted plans.
- Do not persist allocation scores or blocking time.

Acceptance:
- SeasonPlanSchema validates current fixtures and the new seeded workflow data.
- Existing admin assignment and auto-assignment tests remain valid.
- Stable IDs are used for matches, slots, and members.
- Record implementation decisions in the referenced ADRs.
result: Added explicit slot lifecycle, migration from legacy occupancy, capability eligibility, completion-after-closing behavior, and stable fixture migration. Verified with full test suite (84 passed) and typecheck.

name: Allow copying a plan with or without selecting which data to copy
description:
Allow users to create a new plan by copying an existing plan. Provide a simple full-copy path for the common case and an advanced selective-copy path for choosing which data sections to carry over. The new plan must receive a fresh identity and must not mutate the source plan.

Decisions:
- Support both full-copy and selective-copy modes.
- Selectable sections should include members, teams, matches, gamedays, assignments, and configuration where the current model supports them.
- Assignment reset behavior must be explicit before confirmation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Full copy creates an independent plan with a new ID.
- Selective copy previews and applies the chosen sections only.
- The source plan remains unchanged after copying.
- References are valid after sections are omitted or assignments are reset.
- Copy failures leave no partially active plan and show an actionable error.
- Tests cover full copy, selective copy, and source immutability.

name: Add locale key completeness test
description: Add locale integrity coverage for the supported English and German JSON files. The implementation must recursively compare key paths in both directions, handle nested objects and arrays consistently, and report the exact dotted path when a locale is missing a key. It must also statically inspect application TypeScript/Vue source for literal i18n calls such as t("...") and verify every referenced key exists in both locale files. Dynamic translation keys must be handled conservatively without false confidence. Acceptance criteria: current locale files pass; removing a key from either locale fails with the missing locale and exact path; referenced literal keys are validated; no new dependency is required. A separate follow-up task covers migrating hard-coded public UI text and enforcing that rule.
result: Implemented locale integrity coverage. Added recursive English/German key-path comparison with indexed array paths, literal t/$t reference extraction from application Vue/TypeScript source, and missing-reference detection. Added the two missing English onboarding keys discovered by the test. Verification: focused locale test 7/7 passed; app suite 56/56 passed; pnpm typecheck passed; changed files lint clean. Full pnpm lint remains blocked by pre-existing formatting errors in unrelated docs and fixture files.

name: Solve SSE Clobbering in usePlanStore

Prevent remote updates from overwriting local unsaved changes.

name: Create a full example plan and views for data from last season

Provide a realistic, usable example plan so the complete member, event, assignment, and cockpit workflow can be explored without manual setup. The plan is seeded from anonymized historical data and must include the roles, skills, teams, members, gamedays, matches, duties, and views needed by the tracer-bullet flow.

Completed slices include historical data ingestion, people/team views, timeline events, and selected-member/cockpit behavior. The remaining child is the timeline/calendar toggle.

Acceptance criteria:
- Two representative season fixtures validate against the current SeasonPlan schema.
- Example data supports browsing people, events, matches, duties, and personal schedule.
- Seeded roles and skills include explicit capability requirements.
- Timeline and calendar views link to the existing event/match details.
- The example plan is safe to share and contains no production personal data.
- Focused fixture and user-flow tests pass.
result: Completed on main. Both 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 anonymized fixtures validate against SeasonPlanSchema and include seeded skills, capability-bound roles, teams, members, gamedays, matches, and duties. Timeline and calendar schedule views are implemented with links into match details; member cockpit and iCal export are covered. Verification: API tests 12/12 passed, app tests 56/56 passed, E2E tests 31/31 passed, typecheck passed, and lint passed. Nuxt/plugin and expected API error-path warnings remain non-failing.

name: Unsaved Changes (Dirty State) Indicator & SSE Conflict Shield
description:
Protect local plan edits from remote SSE updates and make the conflict visible to the user. This is the single dirty-state task; the older cmvcolty task is superseded by it.

Scope:
- Track whether the active plan has unsaved local changes.
- Show a clear dirty indicator when local state differs from the last persisted revision.
- If an SSE update arrives while dirty, retain local edits, record a conflict, and do not silently overwrite state.
- Provide an explicit user action to reload remote data or keep/retry local changes according to the existing save/CAS behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Local edits set dirty state and successful persistence clears it.
- Remote updates while clean apply normally.
- Remote updates while dirty never clobber local state and expose a conflict state.
- User actions and failure paths are accessible and localized.
- Tests cover clean SSE update, dirty SSE conflict, save success, and save/CAS failure.

name: Fix AES-GCM IV Reuse in use-crypto.ts
description:
Fix the cryptographic flaw where a fixed zero IV is used. 
- Generate a random 12-byte IV for every encryption.
- Prepend the IV to the encrypted blob.
- Update decryption to handle both the new format and legacy zero-IV plans.
result: Superseded when the older security epic was retired during backlog refinement; revisit only as a newly specified current security task.

Member selection belongs to cockpit setup, not fixture detail; claiming without a selected member opens the selection dialog and resumes the claim.

Expand the /guide page into a practical, localized knowledge base for the current product. Explain end-to-end encrypted links, initial setup, teams and members, helper-team assignment, personal schedule and .ics export for Apple/Google Calendar, and mobile duty/check-in behavior. Keep explanations aligned with actual current behavior and clearly label deferred features.

Acceptance criteria:

- Instructions match the current routes and controls.

- Guide is readable and usable on mobile and desktop.

name: Harden plan data model migrations and compatibility
description:
Make SeasonPlan evolution explicit and safe. Older encrypted/shared plans must be migrated on the client immediately after decrypt/load and before entering active state, including shared-link loads, resume/refresh loads, and SSE updates. Keep server-side payloads opaque.

Requirements:
- Define the current schema version once and document supported field/structure changes.
- Add a representative legacy fixture with pre-current omissions such as assignmentStatus and/or gameday slots.
- Test legacy parse, migration, current-schema validation, match duties, and gameday duties.
- Verify current plans remain unchanged and migration does not mutate source fixtures unexpectedly.
- Add a browser test for legacy shared-plan load, fixture/match rendering, eligible claim safety, refresh persistence, and cockpit visibility.
- Keep member-facing concepts to duties/status/progress.

Acceptance criteria:
- Legacy fixture is automatically parsed, migrated, and validated.
- Shared-link, resume, and SSE paths use the same migration boundary.
- Schema version and migration note document any breaking change.
- Browser test proves the required legacy flow.
- Relevant unit, app, API, and browser checks pass.

name: Implement read-only webcal calendar feed
description:
Research and implement a read-only webcal-compatible calendar feed for the agreed member-specific and/or plan scope. Native clients cannot execute app-side key derivation, so do not assume a derived key solves access. Use docs/research/calendar-feeds.md to drive the decision between a query-key endpoint, opaque token, or client-generated projection.

The feed must remain read-only and must not expose the SeasonPlan decryption key as the subscription credential unless explicitly accepted. Define token scope, expiry, revocation, cache/privacy headers, stable UIDs, update/cancellation behavior, timezone serialization, target clients, and acceptable polling staleness before implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- The chosen access model and trust boundary are documented.
- The endpoint returns valid RFC 5545 over HTTPS with stable UIDs and deliberate timezones.
- Missing, invalid, expired, revoked, or unavailable access produces a deliberate response without unrelated plan leakage.
- Focused API/unit tests cover empty plans, malformed dates, repeat requests, and update/removal behavior.

name: Create Page or popup 'this is me' to associate a person within a plan
description: The idea is, that someone, who opens the plan for the first time, can associate themselves with a person in the plan to get a 'for me' page later on with their games and their helper dates.

name: Decide whether schedule import belongs in the product
description:
Evaluate whether the app should import schedules from .ics, CSV, nuLiga, or another source. The topic is mentioned in README.md and dev-docs/user-workflows.md but is not in the current roadmap.

Decision questions:
- Which source formats, if any, are current product commitments?
- What are the timezone, deduplication, invalid-event, and update rules?
- How are existing matches, duties, and assignments preserved?
- Is nuLiga import still intentionally out of scope?

Acceptance criteria:
- Record an explicit include/defer decision and rationale.
- If included, define a follow-up implementation epic with scope and acceptance criteria.
- Update stale references so documentation agrees with the decision.

name: Implement the JSON command runner
description:
Implement the process-friendly runner using the contract from the boundary task and the extracted application operations. It should accept one JSON request, load or receive a SeasonPlan, execute exactly one command, and emit one JSON response. Add the smallest package script or executable entry point needed for local and agent use; do not add a CLI framework unless the existing runtime cannot support the simple interface.

Acceptance criteria:
- Supports validate, claim-duty, auto-assign, and complete-assignments.
- Supports a deterministic clock/input where completion behavior depends on current time.
- Emits stable JSON on stdout and diagnostics only on stderr.
- Returns a non-zero exit code for malformed JSON, unknown commands, invalid plan data, and rejected domain actions.
- Does not import or initialize Pinia, Vue UI code, browser storage, or SSE.
- Repeated invocation is easy to script from shell and agents.

name: Prototype regular and admin navigation variants
description: Build a throwaway prototype comparing two plan-scoped management experiences: (A) a shared plan shell with an explicit admin-mode activation control, and (B) a separate Manage plan shell reached from regular plan navigation. Prototype both desktop and mobile navigation/discoverability paths, including assignments, teams, and setup. Persist the alternatives, observed trade-offs, and rejected option in the task result and linked design notes. Treat admin mode as a UX boundary only, not authorization. Done when the team can choose a variant from the prototype without implementing production behavior prematurely.
result: Documented and prototyped option D: shared plan links land on the current schedule; a persistent, toggleable Edit mode reveals a mobile-friendly Manage dropdown for Assignments, Teams & members, and existing-plan Setup. Recorded the decision in docs/adr/0010-schedule-first-edit-mode.md. Full prototype remains on branch prototype/plan-navigation-variants for evaluation.

name: Enforce i18n for all public-facing UI text
description: Migrate hard-coded user-facing text in app Vue templates and UI-facing TypeScript into English and German locale keys, then add source-level enforcement for future literals. The enforcement should cover template text nodes and user-facing attributes such as placeholder, title, aria-label, and button/modal labels, while allowing documented exceptions for brand names, user-entered data, and domain data such as member, team, and match names. Ensure both locale translations exist and preserve accessibility semantics. Add focused tests or lint coverage and verify the full app suite.

description: Replace the current legacy wizard entry with explicit placeholder pages at /setup and /plans/:planId/setup. Add a clear base-route action to /setup and a clear canonical plan-navigation path to existing-plan setup. The placeholders must state what is unavailable, provide a useful next action, and contain no fallback/example plan behavior. Add route/rendering tests proving both paths are reachable.

name: JSON command runner for plan business logic
description:
Create a small internal JSON-in/JSON-out command runner for plan business logic. Commands operate on decrypted SeasonPlan JSON and reuse the same domain operations as the web UI. The runner is for tests, agents, and local debugging, not a public product CLI.

Commands in this epic: validate, claim-duty, auto-assign, and complete-assignments. The normal workflow is get/read a plan, issue one mutation, then get/read the resulting plan again outside the runner. Mutation responses should therefore be compact summaries/results by default; add a low-priority follow-up for an optional --full mode that returns the complete updated plan.

Boundaries:
- No Pinia, Vue, browser storage, SSE, HTTP API, or remote encrypted-plan access.
- Existing domain rules remain authoritative.
- Malformed input, invalid plans, unknown commands, and rejected domain actions are machine-readable failures with non-zero exit status.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract, domain extraction, runner, tests, and usage documentation are completed in dependency order.

name: Replace SaaS landing with link-first entry flow
description:
Remove the current SaaS-style landing page from the root entry path and make the application link-first.

Canonical URL recommendation:
- General plan: /plans/<planId>#key=<key>
- Match detail: /plans/<planId>/matches/<matchId>#key=<key>

Use the nested match path because a match is a resource within a plan, not a filter or incidental view state. The client must still decrypt the plan before resolving the match, but that does not require putting matchId in the query string. Unknown match IDs must produce a stable not-found state rather than fallback data. The query-string alternative (/plans/<planId>?matchId=<matchId>) was rejected because it weakens the resource hierarchy and makes accidental fallback rendering easier. Keep the decryption key in the URL fragment; fragments are not sent in HTTP requests, but the key remains a bearer secret and is not authentication.

Desired behavior:
- A valid plan link opens the general plan view directly.
- A valid match link opens the specified match detail after the client decrypts the plan.
- A base-URL visitor with no usable link sees a minimal empty state explaining: “Did you receive a link?”
- If a previously opened plan is saved locally, the base URL shows an explicit Resume button.
- If no local plan is available, the empty state does not pretend that a plan exists.
- Remove the SaaS landing page from `/`; do not preserve it as the default experience.

Access and persistence requirements:
- Persist the plan ID and decryption key together in the local resume state, using the existing client-side storage approach and without exposing the key in visible UI.
- Handle missing, malformed, expired, or undecryptable links with a clear recoverable error state.
- Keep the existing setup/admin entry path available where it is still needed, but do not force shared-link users through setup.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fresh base-URL visitor sees only the link-first empty state.
- Shared plan link lands directly on the plan schedule.
- Shared match link lands directly on the requested match detail.
- Returning visitor can reopen a locally saved plan without the original URL fragment.
- Unknown match IDs never render arbitrary or fallback match data.
- Link and resume failures provide a useful next action.
- Existing setup, encrypted loading, dashboard, assignment, and test flows remain functional.
- Record the decision in docs/adr/0001-link-first-entry-and-slot-lifecycle.md.

Out of scope: authentication, public discovery/search, marketing content redesign, and changing the underlying encrypted plan format.
result: Replaced the root landing page with link-first empty/resume state and added canonical plan and nested match routes with encrypted fragment loading and stable unknown-match state. Verified with full test suite (84 passed) and typecheck.

name: Add API CAS concurrency coverage
description:
Add focused API coverage for concurrent plan writes. The save API accepts an encrypted opaque blob plus expected revision metadata; concurrent writes for the same plan must serialize and reject stale revisions with HTTP 409.

Acceptance criteria:

- Exactly one write succeeds and the stale write returns deterministic 409 Conflict.
- Stored data is the winner payload; an existing assignment is not overwritten by the rejected write.
- Client-facing claim failure does not show success and restores local slot state.
- Server tests treat encrypted payloads as opaque.
- Document the process-local lock limitation or use storage-native atomic CAS where supported.

name: Implement member fixture-to-claim-to-cockpit tracer bullet
description:
Implement the first real member-facing workflow in mima using the existing encrypted plan and Pinia store. Read CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/ before implementation.

Flow:
1. Render a data-driven fixture list from the active plan.
2. Navigate to a match detail route using a stable matchId.
3. Render that match's helper slots and current occupancy.
4. Let a selected prototype member claim an open eligible slot.
5. Show the assignment in a personal cockpit view and link back to the match.
6. Persist the claim through the existing plan save path.

Domain behavior:
- Add one shared claim operation at the store/domain boundary.
- Reject unknown match/slot/member IDs, occupied slots, and missing required capabilities.
- Never overwrite an existing assignment.
- Claiming does not mark a duty completed; completion follows gameday closing time.
- Store the selected member ID, not a display name.
- Helper-team membership affects prominent presentation, not eligibility.
- Keep admin assignment behavior working.

Required states:
- No fixtures, unknown match, no selected member, no personal duties, ineligible member, occupied slot, save failure, and unavailable/corrupt local state.

Do not implement swaps, live scoring, authentication, notifications, or external imports as part of this tracer bullet.
result: Implemented shared claim boundary, member selection persistence, fixture and match routes, claim persistence, failure recovery, and personal cockpit. Verified with full test suite (84 passed) and typecheck.

name: Example scenario: isolate mutable E2E plan data
description:
Background: The plan-routing E2E test failed in PR #42 because user-workflows.e2e.spec.ts and plan-routing.e2e.spec.ts shared the same remote seeded plan. The workflow intentionally changed the club name, forced a failed save, then retried without restoring the draft, leaving the plan named "Failed Save Attempt". The routing test asserted the original "Gladbeck HC" heading and timed out even though the route, API, and deployment were healthy. Keep this scenario as a named example for future debugging and test-design context.

Task: Remove shared mutable state between E2E suites. Prefer giving each suite its own seeded plan identity and encryption key, or reset the remote fixture before every suite when unique seeding is impractical. Ensure workflow tests can mutate their plan without affecting routing, accessibility, or other E2E tests.

Selectors: First isolate the data. Add stable data-test-id attributes only to meaningful page-level test seams that are otherwise difficult to identify; do not use test IDs as a substitute for independent fixtures. The routing test should assert a stable page marker or semantic element after isolation, not a mutable fixture value such as the club name.

Acceptance criteria:
- Running the complete E2E project does not depend on file order or shared remote plan state.
- The workflow suite can save "Failed Save Attempt" without changing routing-suite expectations.
- The routing suite seeds or selects an independent plan and passes repeatedly against the deployed test host.
- Assertions use accessible roles/text where stable; any new data-test-id is documented by the behavior it represents.
- Run the full E2E project and record the result.
